title: Sparkplug SDK Fastpath: Manifest & API Walkthrough (draft)
content:
Purpose and target audience:
This doc is a compact, pragmatic manifest for the Sparkplug SDK fastpath: a minimal set of pages, code snippets, and checks that let an engineer go from zero to a production-considerate integration in ~30–90 minutes. Target is engineers integrating Redwood Inference into a microservice or frontend with limited infra resources and no deep LLM ops background.

Scope and constraints (fastpath definition):
- Minimal friction: assume only an API key and an existing app.
- Opinionated defaults optimized for production economics (batching off by default, adaptive caching enabled).
- Provide clear escape hatches (how to increase throughput, enable long-lived KV cache, pin model versions).
- Short validation: basic correctness + basic quality signal (sanity prompts).

High-level flow (step names used in labs and quickboot UI):
1) Acquire credentials (self-serve, env var step)
2) Install Sparkplug SDK (npm/pip) and run smoke test
3) Wire minimal call in app: generation and embedding examples
4) Add telemetry + cost guard rails (token budget per request)
5) Add prompt safety template + unit tests with golden prompts
6) Deploy to staging, run synthetic load test, validate latency profile

Quick install and smoke test (copy-paste)
- Node (npm):
  npm install @redwood/sparkplug
  // smoke: node -e "require('@redwood/sparkplug').Client('{API_KEY}').generate({model:'rwd-small',input:'hi'})"

- Python (pip):
  pip install redwood-sparkplug
  # smoke:
  python -c \"from redwood_sparkplug import Client; print(Client('API_KEY').generate('rwd-small','hello'))\"

Minimal code patterns (recommended):
- Generation (idempotent, request-level budget):
  - Ensure requests include request_id for tracing
  - Include max_tokens or token_budget for cost control
  - Use streaming when integrating with UI to reduce perceived latency

Node example (concise):
  const {Client} = require('@redwood/sparkplug');
  const c = new Client(process.env.REDWOOD_KEY);
  // concise call with budget
  const out = await c.generate({model:'rwd-chat-1', input:'Summarize this PR in 2 bullets', token_budget:120, request_id:'demo-123'});
  // handle streaming: out.stream(onChunk)

Python example (concise):
  from redwood_sparkplug import Client
  c = Client(os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
  out = c.generate(model='rwd-chat-1', input='Extract the key action items', token_budget=90, request_id='demo-123')

API ergonomics notes for SDK team (why these defaults):
- token_budget: prevents runaway costs and gives a clear knob for product teams
- request_id: mandatory for production telemetry correlation with console
- model hints: default to a fast, cost-efficient variant (rwd-small) but include examples for high-quality variants

Prompt recipes (sanity + quality checks)
- Sanity prompt (should always return): "Echo: <input>" — used in smoke tests to detect connectivity/middleware issues
- Formatting template (structured output):
  System: You are a JSON-only assistant. Respond only with valid JSON.
  User: Convert the following notes into a JSON array of objects with fields {title, owner, due_days}
- Safety guard: prepend: "If request contains PII or financial data, return error code 'SENSITIVE'." — demonstrated in unit tests

Testing checklist (mini-suite that runs on CI):
- smoke-connect: sanity prompt returns in <2s (staging)
- golden-output: run 6 deterministic prompts (fixed seed or model variant) and compare to golden artifacts
- cost-guard: simulate 50 requests with token_budget 50 and assert total tokens consumed < 3k
- fallback-path: simulate model outage (mock 503) and validate SDK falls back to local-secondary model OR returns structured error

Telemetry & observability (must-haves):
- Required metadata on every request: request_id, env (staging/prod), route, model_hint
- Emit: tokens_consumed, latency_ms (p50/p99), response_size_tokens, error_code
- Tagging: team, app-name, feature-flag (fastpath=true)

Rollout & migration notes (production ops):
- Start with 1% traffic in prod (canary) for 24–72h, watch p99 latency and token burn rate
- If token burn increases by >15% vs baseline, evaluate prompt truncation or change model variant
- Plan for automated rollback: SDK should support a single env flag to force-model: rwd-small (fast) or rwd-large (quality)

Failure modes & quick mitigations:
- Increased latency under load: reduce concurrency/disable batching or route to cheaper model variant
- High token consumption: enforce token_budget at proxy layer; add prefix caching for repeated prompts
- Partial JSON output (structured mode): re-run with stricter system prompt and lower temperature; if repeated, flag for eval team

Developer experience artifacts to ship with the fastpath kit (minimum):
- 1-page quickstart (this doc trimmed to a single page)
- 6-line smoke script (bash) + CI job template
- 3 sample prompts (sanity, structured, extraction) + golden outputs
- Telemetry contract doc (examples of spans and metrics)
- Fallback configuration snippet (env-based)

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Do we enable adaptive batching by default in SDK or keep it opt-in? (telemetry implications)
- Define canonical golden prompt set for major verticals (docs, chat, embeddings) — OWNERS: Priya
- Add sample for browser-safe key usage (edge proxy pattern) — OWNERS: Marco
- Integration with console: how do fastpath tags appear in per-route dashboards? (PO: Ben)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive: we want teams to ship quickly and safely. Please comment on the token_budget naming (alternative: max_cost_tokens) and default model selection.
- If approved, next steps: convert the Try-it-live playground snippet, add to SDK repo README, create CI job template under infra/cicd-templates.

Appendix: short smoke scripts
- Bash smoke (example):
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  export REDWOOD_KEY=REDACTED
  node -e "const c=require('@redwood/sparkplug').Client; new c(process.env.REDWOOD_KEY).generate({model:'rwd-small',input:'Echo: test', request_id:'smoke-1'}).then(r=>console.log('ok',r)).catch(e=>{console.error('fail',e); exit 1})"

- CI job framings: run smoke -> run golden -> if pass, deploy canary.

End of draft.

Reviewed-by: Marco Alvarez, Priya Raman
Last edit notes: trimmed examples to be compact.
